finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection in /ping: req.query.host is concatenated into a shell command string passed to exec(), so any remote client can run arbitrary commands (e.g. host=8.8.8.8;id or $(...)). Command output is returned in the response.
finding.source: req.query.host (HTTP GET query parameter, no authentication)
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, run via /bin/sh -c

trace.note: GET /ping handler registered with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated unsanitized into the shell command string
stdout returned to the caller, so output is visible to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware, no input validation or allowlist, no escaping, and no argv-array form (exec uses a shell). Other routes (/version uses execFile with constant args; /uptime uses a constant command) were checked and are not injectable.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (a shell) with no auth, validation or escaping, and tools.js:11 returns stdout; one nuance is that a non-zero exit returns 502 with no body (tools.js:8-9), but `;id` still yields exit 0 from the last command and blind injection works regardless.
